newsitem.title: USA: Beanie Babies boost McDonald's April sales.
newsitem.headline: Beanie Babies boost McDonald's April sales.

text.p: U.S. comparable store sales for McDonald's Corp in April increased in the high single digits over the same month a year ago, boosted more by a promotion of Beanie Babies toys than from its 55 cent campaign, analysts said on Friday.

While McDonald's officials declined to confirm the high single digit gains, Brad Ball, senior vice president of marketing U.S.A. said, "April U.S. comparable same store sales were the strongest we've seen in three years."
Comparable store sales exclude results of new restaurants.

McDonald's had planned to give away as a promotion 100 million Teenie Beanie Babies over a five week period beginning April 11. However, overwhelming demand for the small plush animal toys depleted the inventory and the promotion was cut short around April 21.
Earlier in April, McDonald's had launched Campaign 55 offering one of four breakfast sandwiches for 55 cents when combined with the purchase of hash browns and a drink.
"The breakfast business responded rather well in that our goal was to get people to buy meals in combination," Ball said in a telephone interview.
On April 25, McDonald's launched the next phase of Campaign 55 offering its Big Mac hamburger for 55 cents when combined with purchase of any size drink or any size fries.

Ball said that although there are some preliminary indications of increased customer traffic, it is too early to gauge the success of the promotion. "That's a very short time in the Big Mac phase of promotion," he said.

Customer traffic is a key factor in the success of the campaign, said analyst Jeffrey Omohundro at Wheat First Butcher Singer, adding that some negative publicity that franchisees had raised some prices in advance of the promotions hurt the early phase. "It's still fairly early. Breakfast seems to be working, but it's still a little bit early on hamburgers," he said.
